verdict: key consistent: 44 signs = 44 letters of the cipher's text, 13 groups = 13 words (ولابد written as two groups ولا | بد), one letter per shape at skeleton level (S5 = ع in العيش and غ in يغلب); homophones ب (S11, S15), ر (S17, S18); the cipher is the whole line plus a last word مشربا
notes: Rows 7r l.5-8 on image 0084_0018. Signs per row 12,12,10,10 = 44 (record 13,13,11,14 = 51; the segmenter split the heart+ring and 6-shapes); dividers 3,4,3,3 = 13 (record 11; row 8 ends with a divider). Corrections: (1) the plaintext is the whole of l.10 and fits exactly; the record's 'signs > letters' hypothesis (a missing hemistich) is wrong. (2) The word after من is قذا (S13 S14 S3), not هذا: ه is S1 (in هو) and S13 is a different sign; the page has a dotted ق/ف with tanwin (قذًا 'a mote'), giving 'Such is life in this world: there must be some mote that overcomes its clearness or troubles it'. (3) ولابد is enciphered as two groups ولا | بد. (4) The cipher adds a fifth group after يكدر: S12 S7 S18 S11 S3 = م ش ر ب ا, مشربا, the word written small above مترجما in the next heading (l.11, 'وكتب لي فخر الدين عثمان مشربا مترجما'); it may be a label for the kind of cipher rather than part of the verse. Not in the record's plaintext. (5) The ك of يكدر is a U (S20) added above the π in browner ink, apparently a later insertion; keyed as a sign. Label S19 is not used.
